reading.body:
Bill Hagerty's AI record is mostly money and one bill: five-figure-scale PAC checks from Google, Meta, Amazon, and Intel, plus sponsorship of the BLADE Act and a run of votes on S. 2296.

The contributions are small and repeated rather than large and singular. Google's PAC gives $2,500 twice on the same day in March 2025 and again in May 2026. Amazon's PAC gives $2,500 twice in 2025. Meta and Intel appear once each, at $2,500 and $2,000. This is the ordinary pattern of corporate PAC giving, not a signature of any single donor relationship.

The legislative side is thinner than the money side. One sponsored bill, the BLADE Act, whose title targets adversarial distillation, and a cluster of votes on S. 2296 on a single day in October 2025. The votes split within that day, with yeas on some amendments and nays on others, so the record does not reduce to a single position on the bill.

What the data does not show is causation or alignment. It records that contributions and votes exist, not that one produced the other, and it holds no committee assignments, no floor statements, and no spending on data centers, power, or compute. A reader looking for a link between AI money and AI policy will find the two sets of facts side by side here, and nothing that connects them.
